We need to list files in C drive: maybe "dir C:\". Then create a file: "echo > C:\\testing.txt" or "type nul > C:\\testing.txt". But we should be careful: we might want to create the file in C:\. So command: "cmd /c dir C:\\ > C:\\file_list.txt && echo > C:\\testing.txt". But the user didn't specify where to store listing. They just want to list files in C drive and make file called testing.txt. We can do two separate commands: "dir C:\\" and "echo > C:\\testing.txt". Or combine them.

We need to call the tool. We'll produce a single command: "cmd /c dir C:\\ > C:\\file_list.txt && echo > C:\\testing.txt". But the user didn't ask to store listing. They just want to list files. We can just run "dir C:\\". That will output to console. Then create file: "echo > C:\\testing.txt". We can combine: "cmd /c dir C:\\ && echo > C:\\testing.txt". But we need to pass to tool. Let's do two calls? The tool expects one command. We can combine with "&&". So "cmd /c dir C:\\ && echo > C:\\testing.txt". That will list files and then create file. But we might want to redirect output to file. But not necessary.
